summary: MTLS client-cert CN contains non-ASCII characters (emoji) - OIDC introspection/parsing fails causing 401/500 on admin API in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customers on a private VPC deployment with mTLS client-certs are seeing intermittent 401s or 500s when the admin console or scheduled jobs attempt OIDC token introspection. Initial investigation shows the client certificate Common Name (CN) contains non-ASCII characters (the customer's corporate device certs include an emoji as part of device name). The Go TLS/cert parsing path in our private idp-proxy yields an error when canonicalizing the subject CN; that error propagates and causes introspection to return 500, which surfaces as 401/Access Denied for admin API calls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer config: Private deployment with ingress mTLS termination forwarding client cert via X-Client-Cert header to idp-proxy
2) Use a client certificate whose Subject CN field contains a non-ASCII character (e.g., U+1F600 GRINNING FACE emoji in CN) and perform token-introspection against /oauth/introspect
3) Observe idp-proxy logs: parsing error when decoding subject/CN and introspection handler returns 500
4) Admin console receives 500/401 for subsequent requests that depend on introspection -> unexpected 'access denied' for valid service principals
logs: Mar 13 09:12:44 idp-proxy[svc]: WARN certparser: subject CN contains invalid UTF-8 sequence -> error: 'invalid character in name'
Mar 13 09:12:44 idp-proxy[svc]: ERROR introspect: token introspection failed: downstream parse error: unable to canonicalize subject -> returning 500
Mar 13 09:12:44 admin-api[svc]: INFO request: /api/v1/admin/jobs -> received upstream 500 from auth-introspect -> returning 401 to client
Mar 13 09:12:45 ingress[lb]: DEBUG forwarded header X-Client-Cert length=3456
investigation_notes: Support reproduced locally in staging by generating a self-signed client cert where CN contains emoji U+1F600. The upstream Go x509 library accepts the cert for TLS handshake (mTLS completes), but later subject parsing in our custom claim-extractor fails when attempting ToLower / normalization steps that expect ASCII-only names.
Hypothesis A: our claim-extractor runs bytes-to-string conversion with a strict ASCII sanitizer that returns an error on invalid runes, which bubbles up into the introspection flow.
Hypothesis B: an intermediate library used for logging or fingerprinting calls url.QueryEscape or fmt.Sprintf on subject bytes and chokes on multi-byte runes.
Repro coverage: seen on customer prod and reproduced in our staging cluster (private-deploy replicate). Not observed on hosted API (different proxy stack).
Related: INT-4421 is an internal incident tracking an early-stage fix for UTF-8 handling in claim-extractor. PR referenced in related_github_prs adds additional Unicode normalization tests.

Workaround suggested to customer: rotate to client certs without non-ASCII characters in Subject CN and restart scheduled workers. This is low-friction for small fleets but not acceptable long-term for customer device naming policy.
